text: I’m a 33-year-old guy and I go to the gym two or three times a week. I follow a proper full-body program, track my lifts, use progressive overload, and spend no more than an hour there each time. I’ve achieved what I wanted: I look more muscular instead of soft and fat, I’m stronger, and I know strength training will probably help me stay healthier and more capable as I get older. But saying I enjoy it would be a lie. I hate going. My gym is actually great. It’s clean, not too busy, nobody bothers me, and the workouts themselves aren’t especially complicated. I just spend the entire time wishing I didn’t have to be there. I’ve done team sports before and found them much more enjoyable, but they didn’t give me the same results physically. I also notice that when I’m consistently going to the gym, I have much less desire to drink alcohol, which is another big positive. So how do people deal with this? Do you simply accept that it’s a chore you have to keep doing for the rest of your life?
label: question

text: In terms of how you progress with strength training, there's essentially two ways: you add reps, and/or you add weight. For example, if you did 10 bicep curls with 20lb dumbbells this time, next time you do that exercise, try for 12 reps, or try 10 reps at 22.5lbs. If I’m exhausted, perhaps it’s time to draw it back. But, for me, it’s very much about routine, slow increase, and determining what I could do, rather than what I think I should do. I hope that makes sense!!
